cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: Since when has possession of land SOLO ANIMO been recognised — and how long does it last?
cards.back:
Initially only for seasonally used land (summer/winter pastures, SALTUS); already at the beginning of the classical period, Proculus recognises SOLO ANIMO possession for all land.
• Not unlimited, but only with a view to re-establishing CORPUS; probably lost if the possessor (or his people) does not return as planned.
• Cf Ulpian D 41.2.3.11 (Case 48), D 43.16.1.25 (Case 50); Papinian D 41.2.46 (Case 51).
cards.old_front: Seit wann wird Besitz an Grundstücken SOLO ANIMO anerkannt — und wie lange hält er?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: A occupies B's land without permission, with intent to possess. Does A immediately acquire possession?
cards.back:
No. What matters is whether B regains control — then there has been no change of possession; B was possessor throughout.
• A acquires possession only if B makes no attempt to regain control, or if the attempt fails.
• A change of possession only if it is likely to be permanent.
cards.old_front: A besetzt B's Grundstück ohne Erlaubnis mit Besitzwillen. Erwirbt A sofort Besitz?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: Someone returns home to find his house occupied and cannot drive out the intruder by force. What remedies does he have?
cards.back:
Possessory: INTERDICTUM UTI POSSIDETIS, INTERDICTUM UNDE VI.
Petitory: ACTIO PUBLICIANA, REI VINDICATIO.
cards.old_front: Jemand findet bei der Heimkehr sein Haus besetzt und kann den Eindringling nicht mit Gewalt vertreiben. Welche Rechtsbehelfe hat er?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: Ulpianus (Labeo) D 41.2.6.1 (Case 52): B goes to the market without leaving anyone behind to protect his estate; A occupies it. Does B lose possession?
cards.back:
Prevailing view (Ulpian): B loses possession only if he cannot drive A out after his return.
• Labeo: A becomes possessor upon entering, B loses possession immediately — this view did not prevail.
• As long as nobody intrudes, B retains CORPUS despite his temporary absence.
cards.old_front: Ulpianus (Labeo) D 41.2.6.1 (Case 52): B geht auf den Markt, ohne jemanden zum Schutz seines Guts zurückzulassen; A besetzt es. Verliert B den Besitz?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: What does Celsus D 41.2.18.4 (Case 54) say about the occupation of land by an armed band?
cards.back:
The band acquires possession immediately — but only of the part it actually controls, not of the whole estate.
• Similar to Labeo's view (which did not prevail).
cards.old_front: Was sagt Celsus D 41.2.18.4 (Case 54) zur Besetzung eines Grundstücks durch eine bewaffnete Schar?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: Pomponius D 41.2.25.2 (Case 53): The possessor is absent for a longer period; an intruder occupies the estate. When does the intruder acquire possession?
cards.back:
Only when the possessor B makes no attempt to regain control, or the attempt fails.
• During a longer absence, B has possession SOLO ANIMO.
cards.old_front: Pomponius D 41.2.25.2 (Case 53): Der Besitzer ist länger abwesend; ein Eindringling besetzt das Gut. Wann erwirbt der Eindringling Besitz?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: What applies if the detentors or possessor's agents of a piece of land die or leave the land?
cards.back:
The possessor retains possession SOLO ANIMO — probably only until he learns of it and can take measures to re-establish CORPUS.
• Paulus D 41.2.3.8 (Case 65); Proculus D 4.3.31 (Case 66); Pomponius D 41.2.25.1 (Case 61).
• Julian (Africanus D 41.2.40.1): the lessor loses possession if the lessee voluntarily moves away.
• The lessee's heir continues to exercise control for the possessor (Labeo/Iavolenus D 19.2.60.1, Case 60).
cards.old_front: Was gilt, wenn Detentoren oder Besitzdiener eines Grundstücks sterben oder das Grundstück verlassen?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: Is possession affected if the detentor becomes mentally ill or possesses through a sub-lessee?
cards.back:
No — the possessor's status remains unaffected (Pomponius D 41.2.25.1, Case 61).
• Chain of detentors: the sub-lessee holds for the sub-lessor, who as lessee holds for the lessor; an additional link does no harm (Paulus D 41.2.30.6, Case 62).
• If a detentor merely forms an inner ANIMUS REM SIBI HABENDI, this changes nothing.
cards.old_front: Beeinträchtigt es den Besitz, wenn der Detentor geisteskrank wird oder durch einen Unterpächter besitzt?

cards.topic: 27.10. Possession III — Retaining possession of land
cards.front: What happens to possession if detentors or possessor's agents are driven off the land by force?
cards.back:
Possession is lost IMMEDIATELY — probably because this is a drastic, radical interruption of the existing situation (Papinian D 41.2.44.2, Case 51).
• The intruder acquires possession.
cards.old_front: Was passiert mit dem Besitz, wenn Detentoren oder Besitzdiener gewaltsam vom Grundstück vertrieben werden?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 17] Agathon gives Bellona a pearl necklace for safekeeping. When he insults her weeks later, she throws the necklace into a deep lake and tells him it has been stolen. What is the possessory situation?
cards.back:
1. Deposit: Bellona is a detentor (ANIMUS REM ALTERI HABENDI); Agathon is a mediate proprietary possessor.
2. Throwing it into the lake: the necklace leaves every sphere of influence; control (CUSTODIA) is irretrievably lost → Agathon's possession and Bellona's detention end (cf Ulpian D 41.2.13 pr: stones in the Tiber).
• Bellona does not acquire possession (she does not want the necklace for herself).
• Agathon remains owner.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 17] Agathon gibt Bellona eine Perlenkette zur Verwahrung. Als er sie Wochen später beleidigt, wirft sie die Kette in einen tiefen See und sagt ihm, sie sei gestohlen worden. Besitzlage?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 18] Leo's sheep graze on his pasture; a wether jumps over the fence and strays into Marcia's adjoining forest. Marcia finds it, recognises it as Leo's and decides to keep it. Who possesses the sheep and the wether?
cards.back:
Sheep on the pasture: Leo (control in the sense of being able to access them at any time, cf Example 3).
Wether: Leo loses possession when the animal strays outside his sphere of influence (no more CUSTODIA; cf Pomponius D 41.2.25 pr). Marcia acquires original possession when she takes it — she commits FURTUM (knowingly, with intent to enrich herself).
• Leo remains owner (domestic animal, not a RES NULLIUS).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 18] Leos Schafe weiden auf seiner Weide; ein Hammel springt über den Zaun und verirrt sich im angrenzenden Wald der Marcia. Marcia findet ihn, erkennt ihn als Leos und beschließt, ihn zu behalten. Wer besitzt Schafe und Hammel?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 19] Carus spends the summer in the country with his entire household. Daphne breaks into his empty house in Rome and lives there. When Carus happens to return after a few weeks, he notices this but does not intervene. What happens to his possession?
cards.back:
During his absence, Carus retains possession SOLO ANIMO; the intrusion alone does not yet give Daphne possession.
• When Carus notices the occupation and makes no attempt to regain control, he loses possession and Daphne acquires it (Pomponius D 41.2.25.2; Ulpian D 41.2.6.1).
• Carus still has the interdicts (UNDE VI, UTI POSSIDETIS) and the petitory actions; Daphne's possession is flawed in relation to him.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 19] Carus verbringt mit seinem ganzen Haushalt den Sommer auf dem Land. Daphne bricht in sein leeres Haus in Rom ein und wohnt dort. Als Carus zufällig nach einigen Wochen zurückkommt, bemerkt er es, schreitet aber nicht ein. Was geschieht mit seinem Besitz?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 20] Nike (Rome) possesses an apartment building in Naples, managed by her slave Orion. A plague kills Orion; the tenants Pius, Diana and Ismene flee. Only three months later does Nike learn of this and send her slave Solon as his successor. Did Nike have possession throughout?
cards.back:
Yes — if possessor's agents and detentors die or leave the land, the possessor retains possession SOLO ANIMO (Paulus D 41.2.3.8, Case 65).
• This probably applies until he learns of it and can take measures; Nike acts immediately upon learning of it (Solon) → possession throughout.
• No forcible expulsion (that would end possession immediately).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 20] Nike (Rom) besitzt ein Mietshaus in Neapel, das ihr Sklave Orion verwaltet. Eine Pest tötet Orion; die Mieter Pius, Diana und Ismene fliehen. Erst drei Monate später erfährt Nike davon und schickt ihren Sklaven Solon als Nachfolger. Hatte Nike durchgehend Besitz?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 21] Helena leases her estate to Felix. After a year, Felix sub-leases it to Kreon without her knowledge and hands it over to him. Shortly afterwards, Kreon is driven out by Germanic invaders. What happens to Helena's possession?
cards.back:
1. Lease: Felix is a detentor; Helena is a mediate proprietary possessor.
2. Sub-lease: chain of detentors (Kreon for Felix, Felix for Helena) — does not harm her possession, even without her knowledge (Pomponius D 41.2.25.1; Paulus D 41.2.30.6).
3. Forcible expulsion of Kreon: Helena's possession is lost immediately (Papinian D 41.2.44.2, Case 51); the invaders acquire possession.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 21] Helena verpachtet ihr Gut an Felix. Nach einem Jahr verpachtet Felix es ohne ihr Wissen an Kreon weiter und überlässt es ihm. Kurz darauf wird Kreon von germanischen Invasoren vertrieben. Was geschieht mit Helenas Besitz?

cards.front: [Textbook Ex 22] Eros writes to Flora that he is giving her a thoroughbred horse. Flora sends her slave Gripus, who receives the horse from Eros but, instead of returning, flees into the mountains. A week later he and the horse fall into the hands of robbers. Who possesses Gripus and the horse?
cards.back:
1. Letter/acceptance alone: no transfer of possession.
2. Handover to Gripus: Flora acquires possession of the horse ANIMO NOSTRO CORPORE ALIENO (IUSSUM); that Gripus wants it for himself is irrelevant.
3. Flight: Gripus becomes a SERVUS FUGITIVUS — Flora retains possession of him SOLO ANIMO and, since he remains her possessor's agent, also of the horse he took with him.
4. Robbers: they seize Gripus and the horse → Flora loses possession of both; the robbers acquire originally (mala fide — they cannot acquire anything through Gripus).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 22] Eros schreibt Flora, er schenke ihr ein Rassepferd. Flora schickt ihren Sklaven Gripus, der das Pferd von Eros erhält, aber nicht zurückkehrt, sondern in die Berge flieht. Eine Woche später fallen er und das Pferd Räubern in die Hände. Wer besitzt Gripus und das Pferd?
